newsitem.title: INDIA: India shares close higher, break 5-day fall.
newsitem.headline: India shares close higher, break 5-day fall.

text.p: ** (1315 GMT) Indian shares finish higher on select fund
buying in choppy trade
** Bombay share index closes 10.19 points, or 0.24 percent
higher at 4,193.61, breaking five-day slide
** The Delhi index gains 3.09 points to 881.77, CRISIL-500
** Ruling United Front coalition's core committee set to
meet later Thursday to thrash out nagging issues
rocking three-month old government
** Participants seek clues to market direction amid
political factors
Volatile Indian stocks reversed a five-day losing streak in choppy Thursday trade and brokers said the market might face some resistance.

"What has happened is that the market went into a corrective phase," Jaspreet Ahuja, head of sales at Caspian Research told Reuters. "But, people are definitely waiting to accumulate at these levels."
Blue chips fell victim to sharp profit-taking after crossing 33-month highs last week at 4,448.06, with the Bombay index showing net losses in the last five sessions.
"Foreign fund buying was halted due to political worries," said Bharat Iyer, strategist at UBS Securities. "The market had also been overbought, so everybody had to settle trades."
The market's immediate support level would be around the 4,150 mark where fund buying could emerge, traders said.
Shares of Housing Development Finance Corp fell 448.25 rupees to 4,255 after the central bank said foreign portfolio holdings in the stock had reached a 30 percent ceiling.

A planned move by regional Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK) party earlier this week to pull-out from the ruling coalition added to the slide, but players said politics was just an excuse for the correction.

Participants said a crucial core committee meeting of the 15-party United Front government scheduled on Thursday evening to thrash out nagging issues rocking the three-month old government would provide cues to share prices.

Looking forward, continued buying by U.S. based funds which have largely contributed to the 35 percent bull run in Indian stocks in 1997 amid a surging Dow would take prices to higher levels despite minor hiccups on the way, traders said.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average shattered the 8,000 mark on Wednesday after strong corporate profits and mild inflation data combined to trigger a buying frenzy.
--Anshuman Daga, Bombay equities desk 91-22-265-9000
